In Lau, however, there is no qualification to the penultimate stress rule, so it is the second vowel of such a sequence that is stressed when it occurs in penultimate position. Thus we may contrast: NWN 'ráica' 'see it' / LAU 'raíca'; ONO 'ráuta' 'enough' / VBL 'raúta'. [p. 68] ... a word such as raica 'see it' simply conforms to measure-penultimate stress in Lau, as raíca. new_statements.rule_in_words: Stress falls on the penultimate vowel (in Geraghty's terms the penultimate stress rule, which he equates with Schutz's 'measure-penultimate stress', i.e. penultimate mora/syllable of the measure). Lauan (Lakeba-group islands and Vanua Balavu) is singled out as the only Fijian variety where this rule applies without exception: a high vowel after a lower vowel (ai, au, ei, ou etc.) does not form a diphthong, so in penultimate position that high vowel itself carries the stress (raíca 'see it', raúta 'enough'), whereas all other Fijian communalects stress the first vowel of such a sequence (ráica, ráuta).
new_statements.secondary_stress: Not discussed for Lauan; Geraghty 1979 treats primary stress placement only.
new_statements.exceptions: None for Lauan; the point of the passage is that Lau has NO qualification to the penultimate rule. Fn. 34 (p. 185) suggests the Lau assignment (raíca) may be a recent innovation. The communalect note (p. 30) adds that each Lau island 'is said to have its distinctive intonation'.
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level stress in citation forms of isolated words (dissertation examples such as raica 'see it', rauta 'enough'); the 'measure-penultimate' framing (Schutz 1976a) implies the domain is the phonological measure, but Geraghty gives no phrase-level Lauan data. Statement covers LAU (Nayau, Lakeba, Oneata, Moce, Komo, Namuka, Kabara, Vulaga, Ogea, Vatoa, Ono-i-Lau) and VBL (Vanua Balavu group), which together are the Lauan of Glottolog laua1243.
new_statements.identity_note: Geraghty 1979 treats two communalects that together make up Glottolog's Lauan (laua1243): 21) Lau (LAU: Nayau, Lakeba, Oneata, Moce, Komo, Namuka, Kabara, Vulaga, Ogea, Vatoa, Ono-i-Lau) and 22) Vanua Balavu (VBL, rules 'as for LAU'); the stress statement names both explicitly ('Lau (LAU and VBL)'). It is a comparative dialectological dissertation on 38 Fijian communalects, not a Lauan grammar; the Lau stress facts are stated as the exception to the general Fijian diphthong rule. The variety is not Standard (Bauan) Fijian (fiji1243), whose measure-penultimate accent with the diphthong qualification is described in Schütz.

sources.note: Open copy now obtained by the project (laua1243/). Defines the measure-penultimate accent system and diphthong shortening (chs. 36-41, sec. 41.8) that Geraghty's Lau statement presupposes; silent on Lau-specific accent, so context only, but it cites Geraghty 1983a:98-120 for Lau phonology, confirming the published 1983 book carries Lau detail and stays the top works still to obtain.
